title: The Ashvatthama Stratagem
story:
Drona was cutting through the Pandava army, and nothing could stand before him. The Panchalas and the Srinjayas rushed at him in waves, yelling loud and fierce as they came, and his shafts and darts struck them down as fast as they arrived. They were mighty car-warriors, full of might and energy, and though he slaughtered them they were not yet afraid of him; still they came on, and still they fell. The carnage of steeds and men went on like the slaughter of the gods' enemies in some older age, and the sons of Kunti, afflicted with his shafts, felt fear enter their hearts and hope drain out of them. Drona alone seemed enough to undo them all. The day was theirs to lose, and Drona was taking it from them hour by hour.

"He will consume us all," they said to one another, "like a raging fire eating a heap of straw in the season of spring. There is no one who can even look at him in battle. And Arjuna — the one man who is a match for him — will not fight him." For Drona, conversant with the mightiest of weapons, had been Arjuna's own teacher, and Arjuna, who knew the ways of morality, would not raise his bow against the man who had taught him the bow.

It was Krishna who answered their despair — Krishna, endued with great intelligence and devoted to their welfare. "This foremost of all bowmen cannot be vanquished by force," he said, "not even by the gods with Indra at their head. But when he lays aside his weapons, he can be slain even by men. Cast aside virtue, sons of Pandu, and find some contrivance, before Drona of the golden car destroys us all. When his son Ashvatthaman has fallen, he will cease to fight. Let some man tell him that Ashvatthaman has been slain."

It was not the kind of counsel the brothers had expected from him, and it landed among them like a stone thrown into still water. Arjuna would not approve it; he heard the plan and rejected it. Others approved it. And Yudhishthira — the eldest, the one whose word was truth itself — accepted it only with the greatest difficulty. To save his brothers, he would have to become, for a little while, the instrument of a falsehood, and he agreed to carry it. It was the hardest thing he had yet agreed to in the whole war, and he accepted it with his head bowed.

So it was done, in a way that cut the truth down the middle. Bhima, the mighty-armed, took up his mace and slew a huge, terrible, foe-crushing elephant named Ashvatthaman, one that belonged to their own army, to Indravarman, the chief of the Malavas — their own war-elephant, struck down by their own mace, not to win any fight but to make a single sentence true. Then he approached Drona in the midst of the battle, and with some bashfulness cried aloud, "Ashvatthaman has been slain."

The words were true of the elephant that lay dead behind them. They were spoken to a father who would hear them as his son. There is a difference between a lie and a truth told to deceive, and the whole weight of that difference sat in Bhima's voice. Drona had heard a thousand war-cries that day and never once turned from his work, but this one name, spoken low, would do what no weapon on the field could. On the width of a name shared between a man and a beast, the whole battle was about to turn.
reflection: The man who taught Arjuna the way of dharma on this same field now counsels him to lay that virtue aside, and the text refuses to smooth it over: Arjuna rejects the plan, Yudhishthira accepts it only with great difficulty, and the lie is built out of something technically true. The episode leaves the reader standing in exactly that discomfort, without a verdict.
content_note: Battle violence and a wartime deception.
next_story_tease: The battle did not end with Drona; ahead waited Karna, and an arrow meant for Arjuna alone.
hero_scene: In the dust and noise of the battlefield, Bhima lowers his mace beside the fallen elephant named Ashvatthaman while, at a distance, the chariot of the aged Drona waits as the words of his son's death are carried toward him.
visual_elements: the weight of a shared name
